ledger.note: 1054: Rostov-Suzdal is a share of Yaroslav's division (to Vsevolod I, per the rus dossier). The Vladimir-Suzdal page gives 'Established: 1125' and 'Predecessor: Kievan Rus''; no page opened dates the 1054 division, so the year is the end of the rus dossier. The land is the Rostov-Suzdal core plus Vladimir.

1108: Monomakh sends his son Yuri to govern Rostov-Suzdal. 'In 1108 Vladimir Monomakh sent his young son Yuri to govern in his name the vast' Rostov-Suzdal land (infobox 'c. 1108 or 1125'); the Council of Liubech page has the Rostov-Suzdal lands with Monomakh from 19 October 1097. A change of ruling house on the same land.

1125: Yuri Dolgorukiy moves the capital from Rostov to Suzdal; the principality is 'virtually independent'. The Vladimir-Suzdal page: 'moved his capital from Rostov to Suzdal in 1125' (infobox 'Established: 1125'); the Yuri page has the move in 1121.

region.text: the Volga-Kostroma-Unzha-Sukhona north-east Cliopatria adds in 1126

ledger.note: 1126: Cliopatria widens the principality north and east by about 75,700 km2 over the Upper Volga, Unzha and Sukhona. No page opened dates or names this land; the Veliky Ustyug page says Totma was colonized by Novgorod, so part of it may be Novgorod's. Kept as a bridge to Cliopatria's 1126 shape.

region.text: Kiev, which Yuri held as grand prince

ledger.note: 1149: Yuri takes Kiev (September). 'in September 1149 - April 1151, again in March 1155 - May 1157' he held Kiev as grand prince; the page has 'In 1149 he captured it'. The Rostov-Suzdal shape does not move.
1151: Yuri is driven out of Kiev (April) by his nephew Iziaslav.
1155: Yuri regains Kiev (March). 'In 1155, Yuri regained Kiev once again.'
1157: Andrey Bogolyubsky moves the capital to Vladimir. 'His son Andrey (r. 1157-1175) moved the capital to Vladimir'; Yuri 'was poisoned in 1157'.
1157: Yuri dies (May), 'presumably poisoned at a Kievan nobleman's feast', which 'sparked anti-Suzdalian uprising in Kiev'.

region.text: the Ryazan principality under Roman I

ledger.note: 1180: Ryazan becomes Vsevolod III's vassal. The Ryazan page: Roman I ruled 1180-1207 'as a vassal of Vsevolod the Big Nest of Vladimir and died in captivity'; the Vladimir-Suzdal page has Ryazan's forces beaten in 1177 and resistance put down in 1180, 1187 and 1202; the Vsevolod page: 'In 1180 and 1187 he punished the princes of Ryazan by ousting them from their lands. In 1207 he burned to the ground both Ryazan and Belgorod.'

1212: Ryazan is independent again. The Murom page: 'After Vsevolod the Big Nest died, Ryazan became independent, and its ruler took the title of grand prince'; Vsevolod died on 12 April 1212 (15 April on the infobox) and 'divided his territories among his sons'.

1238: the Mongols reach Vladimir. 'Having burnt down Kolomna and Moscow,' the horde 'laid siege to Vladimir on 4 February 1238'; the city was taken three days later and burned (the page dates Kolomna and Moscow only by sequence).

1238: the Sit River defeat ends organised resistance. Grand Prince Yuri II was 'killed during the Mongol invasions of 1237-1238' ('his death at the battle on the Sit' river in 1238'; the Mongol invasion page has the battle on 4 March); 'Yaroslav II (r. 1238-1246) and the other princes submitted to Mongol rule.'

1240: Cliopatria's Rostov-Suzdal row ends and the Mongol Empire's shape covers the land from 1241. The state did not end: 'Alexander Nevsky (r. 1252-1263) was the last prince to reign directly in Vladimir' and the Grand Principality of Vladimir runs to 1389 (Vladimir-Suzdal page); Cliopatria resumes it as Vladimir-Suzdal from 1294. Fx-52 (K02): the land now passes at this dissolve to principality-of-vladimir-suzdal (identity.successors, listed first), which founds in 1241 and is the Mongols' vassal from then; the counterpart was the Mongol Empire before.

wars.name: Yuri Dolgorukiy's wars for Kiev
wars.outcome: Yuri resumed his push for Kiev in 1147, took it in September 1149, was driven out in 1151 by Iziaslav, regained it in March 1155 and held it until his death in May 1157.
wars.note: Dates from the Yuri page ('September 1149 - April 1151, again March 1155 - May 1157'). The same page has Moscow first mentioned in 1147 and fortified in 1156, Pereslavl-Zalessky and Yuriev-Polski founded in 1152 and Dmitrov in 1154, all inside the shape.

wars.name: Sack of Kiev by Andrey Bogolyubsky's coalition
wars.outcome: Andrey 'had Kiev sacked in 1169, leading to political power shifting to the north-east'; in March 1169 a coalition of native princes led by Andrei of Vladimir sacked Kiev (Kievan Rus' page).
wars.note: No territory is shown to change hands; Kiev was not annexed. In 1173 two Smolensk princes captured Kiev and briefly put Vsevolod III on its throne (Vsevolod page).

wars.name: Vladimir-Suzdal's wars on Ryazan
wars.outcome: Ryazan's forces were defeated in 1177 and resistance was put down in 1180, 1187 and 1202; Vsevolod III burned Ryazan and Belgorod in 1207; Ryazan ruled as a vassal 1180-1207 and was independent after Vsevolod's death in 1212.
wars.note: Mirrored in the principality-of-ryazan dossier. The vassalage is the ledger's vassal_start 1180 and vassal_end 1212.

wars.name: Campaigns against the Volga Bulgars
wars.outcome: Andrey's campaign of 1164 started from Gorokhovets; Yuri II defeated the Bulgars in 1220, helped by troops from Murom (Murom page: afterwards 'Bulgar attacks then stopped').
wars.note: No border moved on the pages opened.

wars.name: Vladimir-Suzdal war of succession
wars.outcome: Vsevolod's sons Konstantin, Yuri, Yaroslav and Sviatoslav fought for the throne after 1212 ('the Vladimir-Suzdal war of succession (1212-1216)'); Yury and Yaroslav were beaten at Lipitsa in 1216 and Konstantin divided the principality among his brothers, creating the Rostov, Yaroslavl and Pereyaslavl appanages.
wars.note: The belligerents are the sons of one family inside the one shape; listed so the reviewer can see it was considered. The page has Novgorod removed from Vladimir's sphere after an uprising in 1207 and Smolensk's hegemony there ended in 1221.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Vladimir-Suzdal
wars.outcome: Kolomna and Moscow burnt; Vladimir besieged 4 February 1238 and taken three days later; the Vladimir army destroyed on the Sit River on 4 March; fourteen north-eastern cities sacked; the princes submitted.
wars.note: The Mongol invasion page lists Torzhok, Rostov, Yaroslavl and Pereslavl-Zalessky among the ransacked cities without dates.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened. The northern and eastern edges (the Volga-Unzha-Sukhona land, Novgorod's Zavolochye) and the Ryazan frontier are approximate throughout.

notes: Pages opened (own budget 5: Vladimir-Suzdal, Yuri Dolgorukiy, Vsevolod the Big Nest, Veliky Ustyug and the Mongol invasion page; Council of Liubech, Ryazan, Murom and Kievan Rus' are shared with other dossiers of the batch). SAME STATE AS principality-of-vladimir-suzdal (Cliopatria 1294-1486, Wikidata Q83546): one Wikipedia article ('Vladimir-Suzdal', 1125-1389), but the later row belongs to batch eu-16-g, so the two rows are kept as two dossiers to avoid two dossiers claiming the same Cliopatria shapes; to merge, move that file's keyframes here and run the end to 1389/1486. Cliopatria shape faults: (1) the shape has a hole at Vladimir, Bogolyubovo, Sudogda and Kovrov, which Cliopatria's Ryazan shape holds (the gazetteer also puts Vladimir outside Cliopatria's Vladimir-Suzdal shapes of 1294 and 1363 and outside its Moscow shape of 1314: the hole runs through the later rows, for batch eu-16-g to see); the correction adds a 70 km disc round Vladimir (and the Ryazan dossier removes the same disc); (2) the 1126 growth (+75,700 km2) is on no page, and Totma, inside it, was colonized by Novgorod (Veliky Ustyug page); (3) Veliky Ustyug is outside the shape though the page makes it part of the principality; added from 1227 as a 50 km disc. Not settled: the 1054 division and the 1125 'Established' (Cliopatria draws Rostov-Suzdal separately from 1056); Novgorod's dependence on Vladimir (the page: Novgorod 'removed from Vladimir's sphere of influence' after the uprising of 1207; Smolensk's hegemony there ended in 1221); Nizhny Novgorod (not on the pages opened); the 1241-1293 years, which Cliopatria gives to the Mongol Empire shape. Murom (separate principality, no Cliopatria row) lies outside the shape. The Yuri page has his move to Suzdal in 1121, the Vladimir-Suzdal page in 1125.
